Hybrid resampling with an 'improved' SMOTE whose change is not described, followed by clustering to delete redundant or noisy samples; no comparison with other resamplers stated.

A new weighted oversampling method built on a redefined intuitionistic fuzzy C-means with symmetric relative entropy, compared with various sampling methods.

New image oversampling method using influence functions and weights, SMOTE on features from a modified pre-trained CNN and a DCGAN generator fed with those features; experiments name no other resampler.
Proposes setting SMOTE's k with the Natural Neighbor algorithm (a new way of applying SMOTE-family methods), compared with the same SMOTE variants at default k.
A sequential SMOTE strategy that generates virtual samples from principal-curve class models and prunes them online, compared with SMOTE-based OS-ELM.

Integrates an MLP-based undersampling (MLPUS, called 'a new approach') with MWMOTE; the abstract does not let one tell whether MLPUS is the paper's own or an existing method, and no comparison is stated.
DIR-SMOTE filters minority instances by density and interpolates while perturbing only top SHAP features, compared with nine standard resampling methods.

FCM-KSMOTE is a newly named oversampler with density-based fuzzy clustering, iterative region partitioning, in-cluster oversampling and noise detection; the compared methods are not said to be resamplers.

Data balancing with an improved SMOTE (clustering and natural neighbours) and a GAN with label information and an optimised training loss (a stated change); no other resampler compared.
COAL active learning framework chains clustering-based uncertainty sampling with an unnamed standard oversampling method, no stated change; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.

WGAN-GP trained on SVM-weighted overlap samples with MAML incorporated into training (a modified generative model), compared with advanced oversampling methods.

CluAD-EdiDO is a multiclass scheme of its own: clustering-based adaptive decomposition with editing-based diversified oversampling per cluster; no named comparison.
A gradient-improved deep GAN with a gradient penalty and deep feature matching in the losses plus a data evaluator, presented as an improved GAN; compared only with a diagnosis method.
NDANKA builds a time-series SMOTE with a numerical-differential artificial natural killer cell method (an own SMOTE variant) for earthquake prediction; compared only with prediction approaches.
AE-ELM-SynMin creates minority samples by crossover, mutation and filtering of AE-ELM hidden outputs and decoding them, compared with SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, Random-SMOTE and SMOTE-IPF.
A newly named RL-controlled subspace ensemble sampling algorithm with a dynamic ensemble module mixing under- and over-sampling, details not given; compared with unnamed traditional approaches.
A modified Borderline-SMOTE (NRBSID) hybridizing noise reduction with borderline-only oversampling, parts not shown to be standard; compared with random oversampling.

BRFE-PBKS-SVM improves SMOTE to oversample in Hilbert space with a PSO-adapted over-sampling rate, alongside imbalance-aware SVM-RFE; no comparison stated.

wRACOG is a new Gibbs-sampling oversampler that selects Markov-chain samples most likely to be misclassified, compared with three well-known resampling methods.
SMOTERoF applies standard SMOTE for each tree of an existing Rotation Forest ensemble, presented as the method and compared with RUS, ROS, SMOTE and UnderRoF.
SMOTE-RD adds a relative-density noise filter and density-based sparsity and boundary weights to SMOTE, compared with 7 popular oversampling methods.

A new over-sampling technique that generates minority samples by manifold distance instead of Euclidean distance; no named comparison.

Balances multiclass data by applying standard SMOTE repeatedly, one class at a time, with no stated change; evaluated only by classifier performance.

ADDPC-SMOTE uses adaptive density-difference peak clustering and spatial distribution entropy to set sampling probabilities, compared with SMOTE, K-means-SMOTE, BS-SMOTE, ADASYN and DPC-SMOTE.

Deep instance envelope network with multilayer fuzzy C-means and a minimum interlayer discrepancy mechanism, a new cluster-based oversampler; compared with representative algorithms not said to be resamplers.

Adaptive TreeHive proposes its own selection of informative majority and minority instances to drive over- and under-sampling before tree ensembles, compared with under-sampling and over-sampling.

Multi-scale convolutional GAN with an attention-guided statistical loss (new architecture and loss) for minority attack traffic, compared with baseline and state-of-the-art GAN schemes.

Hybrid sampling chains k-means with SMOTE in safe clusters and instance-hardness-based undersampling, standard parts without stated change; compared with SMOTE-kNN, SMOTE-Tomek, SMOTE and DBSMOTE.

A new sampling strategy that builds balanced samples by raking and relabeling majority attribute values for the minority class; compared with the popular under- and oversampling methods it names.

A new Monte Carlo oversampler that draws from a density interpolated from the bootstrap empirical distribution of the minority class; compared with past algorithms not said to be resamplers.
A new multi-generator GAN blending TMG-GAN and R3GAN with class-specific generators, a dual-branch discriminator-classifier and decoupling, compared with hybrid sampling, SNGAN and TMG-GAN.

An enhanced SMOTE with entropy-based neighborhood calibration is one of three innovations of an IoT intrusion framework; compared only with state-of-the-art approaches.

A deterministic per-attack supplementation coefficient and generation from local medians and extreme values of neighbours without random interpolation (a new allocation and generator); compared with unnamed basic approaches.

A local PCA approach that generates new churn samples (an own generator), compared with linear regression and standard PCA data generation techniques.

Interpolation oversampling applied in an autoencoder latent space and mapped back (an existing sampler in a learned space); compared with existing synthetic-data methods.
ALIS alternates its own important undersampling of majority instances and generation of informative minority instances, each informing the other; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.

Uses a standard SeqGAN without stated change as the oversampler for text, compared with four other oversampling methods.
Designs a balancing step combining a standard WGAN and ADASYN without stated change, alongside a DenseNet1D and Bi-SRU detector; no resampling comparison.

A diffusion model with a CBAM-enhanced U-net and a new minimal noise scheduling (new architecture and training) to augment fault data; no other resampler compared.
